A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the implementation of the NHI Law in Israel has been a complex, multifaceted process that has been influenced by the unique historical, cultural, political and social context of the country.
the Israeli health care reform was a success in that it achieved the goal of universal health insurance.
the Israeli HMOs have responded to the NHI Law and the managed competition it introduced by developing a "strategic repertoires" that include both "market" and "nonmarket" strategies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the implementation of health care reform is a complex process that requires careful attention to how organizations adapt to new policy environments.
the introduction of managed competition in Israel was not simply a top-down process of policy implementation.

policy makers should be aware of the potential for unintended consequences in the implementation of health care reform and that these consequences may be more pronounced in the public sector than the private.
